name: אָשֵׁר
gloss: on the right path; right going
summary: Jacob's eighth son, Zilpah's second, born to him for Leah, and the tribe that came from him, which camped on the north beside Dan and set out last but one in Dan's camp, its host under Pagiel son of Ochran (Num 2:27; 10:25–26). Leah named him with the root's words for the right path: בְּאָשְׁרִי, "In my right going!", and the piel אִשְּׁרוּנִי, "the daughters will call me on the right path" (Gen 30:13), where the secondary sense, happy, follows from the first. Moses' blessing keeps the name with the path: "let him dip his foot in oil; iron and bronze your shoes" (Deu 33:24–25).

evidence.note: Leah said, בְּאָשְׁרִי כִּי אִשְּׁרוּנִי בָּנוֹת, "In my right going! For the daughters will call me on the right path", and called his name אָשֵׁר: the noun אֹשֶׁר and the piel of אָשַׁר together.
The same piel: her sons rise up and call her on the right path (וַיְאַשְּׁרוּהָ).
The plural noun אַשְׁרֵי, "on the right path is the man who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked": the sense Leah's words carry.
The sons of Zilpah, Leah's maid: Gad and Asher.
Jacob: "Out of Asher his bread shall be rich, and he shall give dainties of a king."
Moses: "Blessed above sons is Asher; let him be pleasing to his brothers, and let him dip his foot in oil."
"Iron and bronze your shoes, and as your days, your strength": the foot and the shoe, words of the way.
Camping beside Dan: the tribe of Asher, its leader Pagiel son of Ochran.
Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Asher, Pagiel son of Ochran.
The fifth lot came out for the tribe of the sons of Asher.
The gentilic הָאָשֵׁרִי, "the Asherite", dwelt among the Canaanites, not having driven them out.
Some men of Asher, Manasseh and Zebulun humbled themselves and came to Jerusalem for Hezekiah's Passover.
Anna the prophetess, of the tribe of Ἀσήρ.
Of the tribe of Asher twelve thousand were sealed.

note: Takes a.gj.af (the name, 43 tokens) and the gentilic אָשֵׁרִי "Asherite" (a.gj.ag, Jdg 1:32), which TIPNR lists as a form of Asher@Gen.30.13; TIPNR has one record for the son and the tribe. a.gj.af also holds a place, Asher on the border of Manasseh (Jos 17:7), which is not a person and is not separated out. Glossed from the ashar entry's own senses (אֶשֶׁר "on the right path is…!", the piel "call on the right path", אֹשֶׁר "right going"), with "happy" as the secondary sense, as that entry has it. The form אָשֵׁר is not itself a word of the entry, so no `word` is given. אֲשֻׁרִים (a.gj.ah, Ezk 27:6) and אֲשֵׁרָה (a.gj.aj) are not this name.
